page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 26.0 GB of dedicated system memory, translating to 6.5 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n1-highmem-4 delivers modest processing and memory throughput. In stress-ng tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier, with scores of 1109.89 and 2914.17 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, register in the bottom 10% tier. Database operations, evaluated via Redis SET benchmarks, achieve 2.75 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.82 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-4 provides a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio compared to standard general-purpose instances, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance compute capabilities. Given its weak CPU benchmark results and lack of local storage or GPU acceleration, this instance is best suited for moderate database operations, caching layers, memory-intensive web serving, and lightweight enterprise applications that benefit from a larger memory footprint without demanding high processing speeds.
